clues: This small town lies in the south of Italy. It sits close to Naples, a much bigger city nearby.
High ground keeps this town a bit cooler than Naples. On hot days, that small gap in heat can feel like a gift.
In 1944, a volcano blast tore through this town and wrecked it. Folks built it back up in the years after that dark time.
A law thinker born in this town wrote letter after letter to Benjamin Franklin. They shared big thoughts by post.
This town climbs the west slopes of Mount Vesuvius. That famed volcano, which once wrecked it, still towers close by.
